messages:
ajay: Quick heads-up — reproducible OOM pattern on gptj-6b-int8 when serving with continuous batching + long outputs. Happens on dedicated pools (p4d-like) but not in tiny dev nodes.

ajay: Repro steps: batch_size=8, concurrency=16, max_new_tokens=1024, kv_cache enabled. 10-30% of requests hit OOM within 5m after warmup. Stacktrace attached.

ajay: ```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.23 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 35.12 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 36.20 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  File "/workspace/runtime/server.py", line 412, in handle_request
    output = model.generate(inp, max_new_tokens=1024, batch_size=8)
``` 

sam: ugh. any fragmentation signs? sizes all over the place or steady leak?

ajay: not a leak per-se; free memory drops after large sequences then stays fragmented. tiny spikes in resident set when multiple requests interleave KV compaction and quantized matmul buffers.

maria: could be allocator + int8 kernels allocating temporary buffers that don't get released to OS. Which allocator are you on? jemalloc or default?

ajay: jemalloc on infra image. quick grep: LD_PRELOAD set to /usr/lib/libjemalloc.so.2

chen: two immediate knobs: (1) reduce default max_new_tokens for the gptj-6b-int8 profile to 512 so common requests don't trigger huge ephemeral scratch allocations, (2) enable kv-cache eviction threshold to evict prefix blocks earlier for multi-turn chats. Both low-risk.

sam: also try setting continuous_batching.max_new_tokens_limit = 512 in routing config so per-route can't request >512 by default. We can still allow overrides for enterprise tenants.

ajay: will try both. also wondering if switching to tcmalloc helps — it has better fragmentation behaviour in our past tests.

maria: we saw >20% lower fragmentation with tcmalloc on similar int4 kernels last quarter. But watch p95 latency.

ajay: quick config I'm going to patch:

```yaml
models:
  gptj-6b-int8:
    defaults:
      max_new_tokens: 512
      batch_size: 4
    runtime:
      kv_eviction_threshold: 0.6  # evict when 60% of kv cache used
      allocator_hint: tcmalloc
``` 

chen: for the kv eviction threshold, prefer a dynamic policy: evict_when(fullness > mean_fullness + 2*std) for big chat workloads. But start with fixed 0.6 as experiment.

deploy-bot: Rollout started for config patch gptj-6b-int8/defaults @ajay. Canary target: 5 nodes in eu-west-1. Logs: https://internal.deploy/rollouts/4302 :robot_face:

ajay: Canary ran for 30m, no OOMs observed under same synthetic load (batch8/concurrency16) — sustained 2k QPS equivalent. Memory usage still spikes but is reclaimed more reliably. :relieved:

sam: nice. did latency p95 change?

ajay: p95 +12ms on average, p99 unchanged. cost per-token unchanged.

maria: can you run a mem-fragmentation profile with heaptrack or our jemalloc stats exporter? want to compare before/after switch to tcmalloc.

ajay: will capture jemalloc stats and a tcmalloc run. planning to push follow-up with graphs tomorrow.

chen: if tcmalloc helps, let's gate it behind a feature flag per-model. Some models (large >30B) we prefer jemalloc for other reasons.

sam: agree. follow-up items: 1) update gptj-6b-int8 defaults to max_new_tokens=512 (done canary), 2) KV eviction heuristic A/B test, 3) allocator A/B (jemalloc vs tcmalloc) perf/frag study, 4) if stable, document new defaults in runtime model-profiles.md.

ajay: noted. will create a short eval run and include regeneration quality check to ensure reducing max_new_tokens default doesn't break downstream UX (some apps expect long continuations). If so, we can expose per-client override.

maria: :thumbsup: thanks. appreciate the quick turnaround.

ajay: ending thread — will post follow-up with graphs and jemalloc/tcmalloc dumps.
